ingredients.cook_qty: 1 tbsp chopped, plus a few leaves

instructions: Fill a large pot with 3 quarts of water, add 1 tbsp of the salt, and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the yogurt, 1 tbsp chopped mint and 1/2 tsp salt, and stir until smooth.
Cook the penne in the boiling water until al dente, about 10 to 11 minutes. Drain it well and divide it among 4 bowls.
While the pasta drains, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. When it foams, stir in the paprika and cook for 20 seconds. Take it off the heat.
Spoon the garlic yogurt over the pasta in each bowl and drizzle the paprika butter on top. Scatter a few mint leaves over each bowl.
Put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
Taste a forkful. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Bailey Farms (the lead, no rating shown) pairs penne with a garlic and mint yogurt and a paprika butter poured over the top, which is the heart of yogurtlu makarna. Its version tops the pasta with a spiced meat sauce; this one leaves that out to keep the dish vegetarian, and keeps its 2 tsp mint to 3 cups yogurt ratio, scaled down. Ambitious Kitchen (4.6 from 15) is a meat version of the same idea with 2 cups Greek yogurt and 4 tbsp butter, which sets the amounts here. Heat moves to the table: cayenne is left out of the butter.
